subject: Conditional vs full likelihood, ExpectedN vs RealisedN

messages.author: 0bcb39e1830d7769
messages.subject: Conditional vs full likelihood, ExpectedN vs RealisedN
parts:
Hello everyone, 

I have two questions about secr and would be thankful if somebody could throw some light.

1) I have read about the differences in expected and realized N. I am running into issues as the area I am interested in estimating N over is way smaller than my state space so expected N is less than the minimum number of individuals I detected. Is it accurate to think about expected N as the number of individuals with home range centers in the area of interest while realized N is that plus accounts for individuals whose activity center is outside the area of interest but their home range partially overlaps with the area of interest, and they were detected on this particular realization of the process?

2) I am using camera trap data, and the sex of some of the individuals of my study species is unknown. I am running the hybrid mixture model (hcov=sex) to accommodate missing sex. Can I use either the conditional or maximum likelihood? I am having better luck with conditional but wanted to be sure both are valid. Also, I read about the four different ways to model sex differences of which the hybrid mixture model and CL=T are two, however, the tutorial mentions not to mix them if I needed to compare the models using AIC, but I have seen people using these two together ......secr.fit (Capt, CL=T, hcov="sex",...) 


Thanks

Tashi

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Conditional vs full likelihood, ExpectedN vs RealisedN
parts:
Hello
1. No, that would be a mistake. An appendix to my recent Ecology paper has the title "Realized population size in an arbitrary small region". That may help, but it's rather technical and doesn't really solve anything unless you have telemetry data. The main message is that to estimate the realised population in a small region A you need some way to partition the contribution of each detected animal between 'inside A' and 'outside A'.
2. Yes, use either CL = F or CL = T. Just don't compare AIC for these two methods, and if you use hcov = 'sex' (note quotes) then do it consistently, even with null models (g0~1, sigma~1). secr.fit (Capt, CL=T, hcov="sex",...) is quite OK.
Murray
